name: Wheat
reason: Ideal for Rabi season; thrives in cool weather and fertile loamy soil.
guideSteps: Seed Selection: Prefer HD 2967, WH 1105, DBW-327, or SMW 5174. Treat seeds with Carbendazim 2.5 g/kg.
Land Prep: Prepare a fine seedbed with 2-3 ploughings. Irrigate prior to sowing if soil is dry.
Sowing: Drill seeds at 4-5 cm depth with 22 cm row spacing, using 100-125 kg/ha.
Fertilizers: Apply DAP 100 kg/ha and Potash 50 kg/ha at sowing, then topdress Urea.
Irrigation: Focus on critical watering stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI), tillering, flowering, and grain-fill.
Harvest: Cut the crop in March-April when stalks turn golden-yellow and grains are hard.

name: Rice
reason: Great for monsoon season; requires high water and heavy alluvial/clayey soils.
guideSteps: Seed Selection: Use IR8, Sonalika, Basmati 370, or Pusa 1121. Treat with Carbendazim.
Nursery: Raise seedlings for 25-30 days while preparing puddled main field with standing water.
Transplantation: Transplant seedlings in rows with 20 cm spacing to ensure airflow.
Fertility: Apply NPK 120:60:40 kg/ha and Zinc Sulfate 25 kg/ha. Split Nitrogen applications.
Watering: Maintain 5 cm standing water until grains ripen; drain 10-12 days before harvest.
Harvesting: Reclaim grains when golden and moisture content reaches 18-20%.

name: Maize
reason: Requires well-drained fertile soils and warm monsoon weather.
guideSteps: Seed Choice: Pick Pioneer 3302, Dekalb 9108, or Syngenta NK6240 hybrid seeds.
Sowing: Spacing at 60 cm x 20 cm at 3-5 cm depth in well-tilled soil.
Fertility: Split Urea into three applications (basal, knee-high, and pre-tasseling).
Pest Alert: Scan for Fall Armyworm regularly. Apply Bacillus thuringiensis if damage is seen.
Irrigation: Keep field moist during critical knee-high and silking phases.
Harvest: Harvest when cob sheaths dry to brown and kernels become hard.

name: Barley
reason: Strong Rabi option for lighter soils and lower irrigation needs.
guideSteps: Preparation: Plow 2-3 times to prepare a clean, fine weed-free seedbed.
Sowing: Sow seeds at 22 cm row spacing and 4-5 cm depth using a seed drill.
Irrigation: Give only 2-3 waterings. Focus on tillering and booting stages.
Weed Control: Spray Pendimethalin 3 days post-sowing to suppress early winter weeds.
Harvesting: Reap when stems are dry and straw turns brittle-yellow.

name: Bajra
reason: Highly suitable for dry regions with sandy soils and low rainfall.
guideSteps: Variety selection: Use drought-resistant hybrid bajra seeds (e.g. HHB 67, MH 179).
Sowing: Direct sow at a shallow depth of 2 cm. Spacing should be 45 cm x 15 cm.
Weeding: Hoeing and weeding at 20-25 days after sowing is critical.
Watering: Can be grown rainfed; provide supplemental watering at flowering if rain fails.
Harvest: Harvest when grain moisture falls below 20% and seed heads dry out.

name: Jowar (Sorghum)
reason: Excellent drought-tolerant crop suitable for black cotton and clay loam soils.
guideSteps: Varieties: Pick CSH-14 or CSV-15 and treat seeds to avoid grain mold and shoot fly.
Soil: Prepare land well. Clayey or black soils are ideal as they retain moisture.
Sowing: Space rows at 45 cm. Maintain plant-to-plant distance at 12-15 cm.
Harvest: Cut the panicles when the grains have hardened and show a black spot at the base.

name: Ragi (Finger Millet)
reason: Highly nutritious millet; extremely hardy in red laterite and sandy soils.
guideSteps: Preparation: Sow in nursery or direct sow. Transplanting gives higher yields.
Nutrition: Apply FYM (Farm Yard Manure) at 4 tonnes/acre during field preparation.
Weeding: Hand-weed twice at 20 and 40 days to keep the crop clean.
Harvest: Harvest in two stages. First cut the earheads, then cut the stalks.

name: Gram (Chickpea)
reason: Pulse crop with high nitrogen fixing; thrives in dry Rabi soils.
guideSteps: Varieties: Select Pusa-362 or RVG-202. Treat seeds with Rhizobium culture.
Planting: Sow in October-November in rows spaced 30 cm apart.
Irrigation: Critical watering at branching and pod-filling. Do not overwater.
Harvesting: Reap when plants dry out, turn brown, and pods rattle when shaken.

name: Moong Dal
reason: Fast summer pulse crop that naturally fixes nitrogen, restoring soil health.
guideSteps: Variety selection: Choose SML 668 or IPM 02-3 for short duration summer growth.
Sowing: Broadcast or drill seeds in mid-March to April, spacing 25 cm x 10 cm.
Nutrition: Requires minimal nitrogen. Apply Phosphorus to encourage root nodules.
Harvest: Pick mature pods in 2-3 pickings as they ripen asynchronously.

name: Urad Dal
reason: Quick-maturing black gram pulse suitable for Rabi rice-fallow or Kharif season.
guideSteps: Variety: Select T-9 or Shekhar-2. Seed treatment with Trichoderma is suggested.
Spacing: Row spacing of 30 cm, plant spacing of 10 cm. Drill at 3-4 cm depth.
Watering: Typically rainfed. Supplement during extreme dry spells at flowering.
Harvest: Cut the crop when 80% of the pods turn black and dry.

name: Arhar (Pigeon Pea)
reason: Deep-rooted pulse crop that withstands drought and improves soil fertility.
guideSteps: Variety: Use UPAS-120 or Pusa-992. Treat seeds with rhizobial culture.
Sowing: Plant in June-July. Space widely (60 cm x 15 cm) due to branching habit.
Weeding: Perform two hand weedings within the first 45 days to control competitor weeds.
Harvest: Cut entire plants when pods turn brown; stack in bundles to dry before threshing.

name: Lentil (Masoor)
reason: Cold-hardy Rabi pulse that grows well in clay-loam and alluvial soils.
guideSteps: Variety: Choose Pusa Vaibhav or K-75. Treat with Rhizobium before sowing.
Sowing: SOW in late October or November with 30 cm row spacing.
Watering: Typically requires 1-2 light irrigations if winter rains fail.
Harvest: Cut close to the ground when plants turn golden-brown and dry.

name: Potato
reason: High-value crop with strong market demand; suits cool Rabi weather.
guideSteps: Seed Selection: Use disease-free seed tubers like Kufri Bahar or Kufri Pukhraj.
Planting: Plant tuber pieces on ridges spaced 60 cm apart.
Earthing Up: Pile soil around the stem base at 30 days to protect tubers from sunlight.
Fungal Control: Apply Mancozeb or Copper Oxychloride to prevent Early/Late Blight.

name: Onion
reason: High demand horticultural crop; thrives in cool Rabi seasons.
guideSteps: Sowing: SOW seeds in nursery bed, transplant seedlings after 6-8 weeks.
Soil preparation: Add well-rotted FYM and compost to get fine, loose loam.
Watering: Stop watering 10-15 days before harvesting to allow drying.
Harvest: Lift bulbs when 50% of the leaf tops drop naturally.

name: Tomato
reason: High-value crop requiring drip irrigation and warm Zaid temperatures.
guideSteps: Transplanting: Shift seedlings to main field after 4 weeks. Plant on raised beds.
Staking: Tie plants to wooden stakes to keep fruits off the wet soil.
Irrigation: Keep soil consistently moist; uneven watering causes blossom-end rot.

name: Carrot
reason: Requires loose, stone-free sandy loam soil to grow straight, sweet roots.
guideSteps: Land Prep: Remove stones and clods. Till deep to create light, loose sandy-loam.
Sowing: SOW directly in ridges, thin seedlings to 5 cm spacing at 3 weeks.
Harvest: Harvest when the root shoulder diameter reaches 2-3 cm.

name: Garlic
reason: High-value bulb crop requiring cool winter climate and fertile soils.
guideSteps: Planting: Separate cloves from healthy bulbs. Plant pointed end up, 5 cm deep.
Earthing: Keep soil weed-free. Shallow hoeing is crucial to protect shallow roots.
Harvest: Lift garlic when 60% of leaves turn yellow-brown and dry.

name: Cabbage
reason: Cold-hardy cole vegetable requiring moist loam soil and regular nitrogen feeding.
guideSteps: Seedlings: Raise seeds in nursery beds; transplant when 4-5 leaves form.
Watering: Requires constant moderate moisture; dryness causes head splitting.
Harvest: Cut heads when they are firm, heavy, and compact.

name: Cauliflower
reason: Demands rich, moisture-retaining loam soils and careful head protection (blanching).
guideSteps: Transplanting: Spacing 60 cm x 45 cm. Transplant late afternoon.
Blanching: Fold outer leaves over the developing curd to protect it from yellowing in sun.
Harvest: Cut when curds are compact, white, and fully developed.

name: Mango
reason: Horticultural orchard crop suited to warm climate and deep alluvial/laterite soils.
guideSteps: Planting: Dig 1m x 1m pits. Mix topsoil with FYM and plant grafted saplings.
Irrigation: Drip irrigation is highly recommended during early vegetative years.
Harvesting: Pick mature fruits when color shifts to pale yellow; wash and ripen in hay.

name: Watermelon
reason: Grows best in sandy riverbed soils and high summer heat.
guideSteps: Sowing: SOW directly in light, sandy soil under high sun exposure.
Watering: Drip irrigate weekly; restrict watering close to harvest to sweeten fruits.
Harvest: Mature melons sound hollow when tapped and the bottom patch turns yellow.

name: Banana
reason: Requires high humidity, abundant water, and well-drained clay loam/alluvial soils.
guideSteps: Saplings: Use tissue culture plants like Grand Naine for disease-free high yield.
Nutrition: Heavy feeder; apply copious compost and split nitrogen/potassium doses.
Harvest: Cut bundles when green fruits turn plump and ribs become round.

name: Orange
reason: Perennial citrus crop; performs well in cool winters and well-drained sandy loams.
guideSteps: Soil: Deep, loose sandy loam is perfect. Citrus cannot stand waterlogged roots.
Pruning: Keep trees clean; prune deadwood to allow sunlight into the canopy.
Harvest: Pluck fruits when they turn bright orange and feel heavy.

name: Apple
reason: Cold climate crop limited to hilly/mountain slopes and loamy soils.
guideSteps: Location: Thrives in temperate zones with chill hours. Plant in winter.
Pruning: Strict winter pruning is necessary to shape trees and induce fruit spurs.
Harvest: Pick hand-sorted when color develops fully and seeds turn brown.

name: Grapes
reason: Vining crop requiring structured trellises and warm, dry climate.
guideSteps: Trellising: Train vines onto telephone or Y-trellis systems.
Pruning: Twice-yearly pruning (October and April) is key to fruit yield.
Harvest: Harvest bunches when berries taste sweet and pedicels turn woody.

name: Papaya
reason: Fast fruit crop requiring warm climate and sandy loam with excellent drainage.
guideSteps: Seedlings: Raise seeds in polybags, transplant at 45 days. Use bisexual strains (e.g. Red Lady).
Drainage: Extremely sensitive to waterlogging, which causes root rot. Plant on mounds.
Harvest: Harvest when skin color shows a light yellow streak.

name: Spinach (Palak)
reason: Fast growing green leafy vegetable; thrives in cool winter climate.
guideSteps: Sowing: SOW directly in lines 20 cm apart. Keep soil moist for germination.
Cuts: Harvest by cutting leaves above root level. Allow to grow back for 2-3 cuts.
Nutrition: Apply nitrogen (Urea) after each cut to boost leaf regrowth.

name: Okra (Bhindi)
reason: Warm-season crop growing successfully in well-drained loamy soils.
guideSteps: Sowing: Soak seeds overnight. Sow in rows spaced 45 cm apart.
Pests: Highly susceptible to yellow vein mosaic virus. Manage whiteflies.
Harvest: Pick tender green pods every alternate day before they become woody.

name: Fenugreek (Methi)
reason: Rapid growth leafy crop; needs cool weather and minimal watering.
guideSteps: Planting: Broadcast seeds. Rake soil lightly to cover them.
Irrigation: Keep soil moist but avoid waterlogging. Highly drought tolerant.
Harvest: Pull out entire plants or cut leaves at 30 days for greens.

name: Coriander (Dhania)
reason: Leafy aromatic crop that thrives in cool winter temperatures.
guideSteps: Preparation: Crush coriander seeds into halves before sowing to speed up germination.
Watering: Maintain light moisture; wet conditions encourage root rot.
Harvest: Cut leaves at 40-50 days when greens are lush and before flowering.

name: Sugarcane
reason: Perennial crop yielding high profits under abundant water and deep soils.
guideSteps: Planting: Trench planting in deep soils. Treat sets with Carbendazim.
Earthing: Keep soil weed-free. earth-up at 4 months to prevent lodging.
Harvest: Harvest when lower leaves dry and cane sugars register high brix.

name: Cotton
reason: Performs well in deep black cotton soils with moderate rainfall and strong sunshine.
guideSteps: Variety: Use Bt cotton hybrids. Plant on ridges to prevent water ponding.
Nutrition: heavy potassium demand at boll stage to support fiber quality.
Harvest: Pluck opened cotton bolls cleanly, avoid dry leaf contamination.

name: Jute
reason: Thrives in warm, humid climates and heavy alluvial deltaic silt soils.
guideSteps: Sowing: Broadcast seeds in April-May. Thin out seedlings to 10 cm.
Retting: Bundle harvested stalks, submerge in clean slow-flowing water for 15 days.
Extraction: Hand-strip fibers from retted stalks, wash, and dry under shade.

name: Sesame (Til)
reason: Warm oilseed crop thriving in dry, light sandy soils with minimal rain.
guideSteps: Planting: SOW seeds shallow (1 cm deep) mixed with dry sand to ensure even spacing.
Water: Keep field dry; standing water causes immediate crop loss.
Harvest: Cut plants when leaves turn yellow and pods at the base begin to open.

name: Sunflower
reason: Highly adaptive oilseed crop; grows well in deep, moisture-retaining soils.
guideSteps: Soil: Deep clay-loams or black cotton soils are best to support heavy heads.
Protection: Protect flowers from birds during seed hardening phase.
Harvest: Harvest when the back of the seed heads turn lemon yellow.

name: Ginger
reason: High-value spice requiring rich loamy soils and warm, humid conditions.
guideSteps: Seed: Use healthy, disease-free seed rhizomes with at least 1-2 active eyes.
Planting: Plant in raised beds to ensure water drains away immediately.
Mulching: Apply green leaf mulch immediately after planting to protect soil moisture.

name: Tea
reason: Requires acid-rich laterite soils on well-drained mountain slopes and warm climate.
guideSteps: Establishment: Plant saplings on contour lines of sloping, well-drained land.
Nutrition: Regularly apply nitrogen and organic fertilizers to boost foliage.
Plucking: Pluck 'two leaves and a bud' every 7-10 days during flushes.

name: Coffee
reason: Requires shade and deep loamy laterite soil with well-distributed rain.
guideSteps: Shade: Plant shade trees (e.g. silver oak) prior to planting coffee.
Blossom: Blossom shower irrigation triggers even flowering across trees.
Harvest: Hand-pick deep red ripe berries; pulp and dry immediately.
